s281.content:
Jadwiga was crowned "King" of Poland at about ten. For her country’s sake she married Jogaila, Grand Duke of Lithuania, who was baptized and became King Władysław II, beginning the conversion of Lithuania.

She founded hospitals, supported the poor, and left her jewels to restore the University of Kraków. She died at twenty-five after childbirth. Pope St. John Paul II canonized her in 1997.
s281.intercession: St. Jadwiga, pray for us. Help leaders to sacrifice for the common good, and bless the peoples of Poland and Lithuania. Amen.

s282.content:
Lidwina was a Dutch girl from Schiedam who broke a rib in a fall while ice skating at fifteen. The injury led to an illness that left her bedridden and in pain for thirty-eight years.

At first she despaired, but a priest taught her to unite her sufferings with Christ’s Passion. She became known for her prayer, mystical gifts, and wise counsel to many visitors. She is the patron of ice skaters and the chronically ill.
s282.intercession: St. Lidwina, pray for us. Give patience and peace to all who suffer long illness, and help them to unite their pain with Christ. Amen.

s283.content:
Colette was a French carpenter’s daughter who lived as an anchoress walled into a cell beside a church until a vision called her to reform the Poor Clares.

With papal approval, she restored St. Clare’s rule of strict poverty and founded or reformed seventeen convents, despite fierce opposition. Her nuns are still called Colettines. She is invoked by women hoping to conceive and by expectant mothers.
s283.intercession: St. Colette, pray for us. Bless mothers and those who long to be mothers, and renew our love of poverty and prayer. Amen.

s284.content:
Francis became a hermit in Calabria at fifteen. Followers gathered around him, and he founded the Order of Minims, whose members kept a perpetual Lenten fast as a sign of humility.

A famous miracle tells that, refused passage across the Strait of Messina, he spread his cloak on the water and sailed across. The dying King Louis XI of France called him to his side. He is a patron of sailors.
s284.intercession: St. Francis of Paola, pray for us. Teach us humility and penance, and protect all who travel by sea. Amen.

s285.content:
John was a Polish priest and professor of theology at the University of Kraków for many years. He was famous for his generosity: he gave away his clothes and food to the poor and often slept on the floor.

He made four pilgrimages to Rome on foot. A saying attributed to him runs: "Fight all error, but do it with good humor, patience, kindness, and love."
s285.intercession: St. John Cantius, pray for us. Bless teachers and students, and help us to combine love of truth with kindness. Amen.

s286.content:
Cajetan was a lawyer and papal official in Rome who became a priest. Distressed by the worldliness of the clergy, he co-founded the Theatines, priests who lived in poverty and relied wholly on God’s providence, not even begging.

He also founded hospitals and charitable pawnshops that lent to the poor at little or no interest. In Argentina and elsewhere he is invoked by those seeking work.
s286.intercession: St. Cajetan, pray for us. Help all who are looking for work, and teach us to trust in God’s providence. Amen.

s287.content:
Jerome was a Venetian soldier who was captured and chained in a dungeon. He prayed to Our Lady, and after his escape he gave his life to God.

During a time of plague and famine he took in orphans, then founded the Somascan Fathers to care for orphans and the poor. He died of plague caught while nursing the sick. He is the patron of orphans and abandoned children.
s287.intercession: St. Jerome Emiliani, pray for us. Protect orphans and abandoned children, and give them loving homes. Amen.

s288.content:
Francis was the Duke of Gandía, a great-grandson of Pope Alexander VI, and a favorite of Emperor Charles V. When he saw the decaying body of the beautiful Empress Isabella, he resolved never again to serve a mortal master.

After his wife’s death he became a Jesuit and later the order’s third superior general, founding colleges and sending missionaries around the world. He is invoked against earthquakes.
s288.intercession: St. Francis Borgia, pray for us. Help us to seek what lasts forever, and to serve the King who never dies. Amen.

s289.content:
Peter was a Spanish Franciscan known for extraordinary penance: he slept only an hour and a half a night, sitting up, and ate once every three days.

He led a reform of the Franciscans and was a spiritual adviser to St. Teresa of Ávila, encouraging her reform of the Carmelites. His little Treatise on Prayer and Meditation was widely read. He is a patron of Brazil.
s289.intercession: St. Peter of Alcantara, pray for us. Teach us self-denial and perseverance in prayer. Amen.

s290.content:
Nicholas was an English carpenter and Jesuit lay brother who spent nearly twenty years building ingenious hiding places for priests in Catholic houses during the persecution. Many of his "priest holes" were never found, and some still exist.

Arrested in 1606, he was tortured on the rack until he died, without betraying anyone. He is a patron of illusionists and escape artists.
s290.intercession: St. Nicholas Owen, pray for us. Bless craftsmen, and help us to protect those in danger for the faith. Amen.

s291.content:
Fidelis was a German lawyer known as "the poor man’s lawyer" because he took the cases of those who could not pay. Disgusted by corruption in the courts, he became a Capuchin friar.

He was sent to preach to Calvinists in the Swiss region of Graubünden, where many returned to the Church. He was killed by an armed mob after preaching. He is a patron of lawyers.
s291.intercession: St. Fidelis, pray for us. Help lawyers to serve justice and the poor, and give us courage to preach the truth with charity. Amen.

s292.content:
Josaphat Kuntsevych was a Ruthenian monk and archbishop of Polotsk, in today’s Belarus. He worked tirelessly for the union of the Eastern Churches of the region with Rome, achieved at the Union of Brest in 1596, while preserving their own Byzantine liturgy.

His opponents saw the union as a betrayal, and a mob killed him in Vitebsk. He was the first Eastern Catholic saint to be formally canonized.
s292.intercession: St. Josaphat, pray for us. Heal the wounds between Christians of East and West, and make us one in Christ. Amen.

s293.content:
Lawrence was an Italian Capuchin friar with a remarkable gift for languages, including Hebrew, Greek, and German, and a deep knowledge of Scripture. He preached across Europe and served as a diplomat for the pope.

In 1601 he led the Christian army at the Battle of Székesfehérvár in Hungary, riding in front carrying only a crucifix. He was named a Doctor of the Church in 1959.
s293.intercession: St. Lawrence of Brindisi, pray for us. Give us a deep love of Scripture and the courage to follow Christ into every battle. Amen.

s294.content:
Joseph was a Spanish priest who came to Rome and was shocked by the number of poor children roaming the streets without schooling. In 1597 he opened the first free public school in Europe.

His Piarist Fathers spread across Europe. He was a friend of Galileo and allowed his teachers to study science. In old age he endured betrayal and the suppression of his order, which was later restored. He is the patron of Christian schools.
s294.intercession: St. Joseph Calasanz, pray for us. Bless schools and teachers, and give every child the chance to learn. Amen.

s295.content:
Mariana was an orphan from a noble family in Quito who lived as a hermit in her sister’s house, devoting herself to prayer, penance, and care for the poor and indigenous people.

During a devastating earthquake and epidemic in 1645, she publicly offered her life to God for the people of Quito. She died soon after, and the disasters ceased. She is called the "Lily of Quito" and is a national heroine of Ecuador.
s295.intercession: St. Mariana, Lily of Quito, pray for us. Bless the people of Ecuador, and teach us to offer our lives for others. Amen.

s296.content:
Claude was a French Jesuit sent as superior to the small community at Paray-le-Monial, where he became the spiritual director of St. Margaret Mary Alacoque and confirmed her visions of the Sacred Heart.

He later served as chaplain to the Duchess of York in London, was imprisoned during the anti-Catholic panic of the "Popish Plot," and was expelled, dying soon after. His Act of Confidence in God is still widely prayed.
s296.intercession: St. Claude, pray for us. Teach us perfect confidence in the Heart of Jesus. Amen.

s297.content:
Oliver was archbishop of Armagh and primate of all Ireland during the persecution of Catholics. He worked to restore the Church, confirmed thousands, and founded schools, often in hiding.

Falsely accused of plotting a French invasion during the "Popish Plot," he was tried in London and hanged, drawn, and quartered at Tyburn, forgiving his enemies. He was the last Catholic martyr executed at Tyburn.
s297.intercession: St. Oliver Plunkett, pray for us. Bring peace and reconciliation to Ireland, and help us to forgive those who wrong us. Amen.

s298.content:
Leonard was an Italian Franciscan who preached hundreds of parish missions across Italy over more than forty years, sometimes to crowds of tens of thousands.

He was the great promoter of the Stations of the Cross, setting them up in over five hundred places, including the Colosseum in Rome. He also promoted devotion to the Sacred Heart, the Blessed Sacrament, and the Immaculate Conception.
s298.intercession: St. Leonard, pray for us. Help us to walk the Way of the Cross with Jesus each day. Amen.

s299.content:
Clement was a baker’s apprentice and hermit before becoming the first Redemptorist priest from north of the Alps. In Warsaw he and his companions kept their church busy from dawn to night with Masses, sermons, and works of charity for twenty years.

Expelled by Napoleon, he went to Vienna, where his preaching, confessions, and friendship with students and artists renewed Catholic life. He is called the "Apostle of Vienna."
s299.intercession: St. Clement Mary Hofbauer, pray for us. Make us tireless in proclaiming the Gospel, whatever obstacles arise. Amen.

s300.content:
Madeleine Sophie was the daughter of a French barrel maker, educated rigorously by her older brother. In 1800, after the turmoil of the French Revolution, she founded the Society of the Sacred Heart to educate girls.

She led the society for sixty-three years, and at her death it had schools in many countries, including the one St. Rose Philippine Duchesne founded in America.
s300.intercession: St. Madeleine Sophie, pray for us. Bless all who educate young people, and make their schools places where the Heart of Jesus is known. Amen.

s301.content:
Vincent was a Roman priest who believed that every baptized Christian is called to be an apostle. He founded the Union of Catholic Apostolate, joining priests, religious, and laypeople in a common mission.

He heard confessions day and night, cared for the sick during a cholera epidemic, and started schools for workers. His vision anticipated the Second Vatican Council’s teaching on the lay apostolate.
s301.intercession: St. Vincent Pallotti, pray for us. Help every Christian to recognize their call to be an apostle of Jesus. Amen.

s302.content:
Joseph was a small priest with a twisted spine who taught moral theology to young priests in Turin and was spiritual director of St. John Bosco.

He visited prisoners constantly and accompanied about sixty condemned men to the gallows, all of whom died reconciled with God. He called them his "hanged saints." He is a patron of prisoners and prison chaplains.
s302.intercession: St. Joseph Cafasso, pray for us. Bless prisoners and those condemned to death, and give them hope in God’s mercy. Amen.

s303.content:
Peter Julian was a French priest who joined the Marists and grew so devoted to the Eucharist that he founded the Congregation of the Blessed Sacrament, dedicated to perpetual adoration.

He also founded a women’s congregation and worked to prepare poor adults for First Communion. He is called the "Apostle of the Eucharist."
s303.intercession: St. Peter Julian Eymard, pray for us. Draw us to adore Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament. Amen.

s304.content:
Maria Domenica Mazzarello was a farm girl from Mornese in northern Italy who, after nearly dying of typhoid, devoted herself to teaching poor girls a trade and the faith.

St. John Bosco chose her to help found the Daughters of Mary Help of Christians, the Salesian Sisters, in 1872. She led them with joy and simplicity, and they now serve young people worldwide.
s304.intercession: St. Mary Mazzarello, pray for us. Bless young women, and help us to serve with joy. Amen.

s305.content:
Conrad was a Bavarian farmer’s son who became a Capuchin brother and served for forty-one years as porter of the friary at the great Marian shrine of Altötting.

He greeted thousands of pilgrims, beggars, and children with kindness, often giving away food. In spare moments he prayed in a small room facing the tabernacle. He is a patron of porters and receptionists.
s305.intercession: St. Conrad, pray for us. Help us to welcome everyone who comes to our door as Christ. Amen.

s306.content:
Joseph was a priest of Turin who was deeply shaken when a poor pregnant woman died after being refused care by every hospital. He opened a small refuge for the sick poor.

It grew into the "Little House of Divine Providence," caring for thousands of sick, disabled, and abandoned people, sustained entirely by donations and prayer. It still serves in Turin today.
s306.intercession: St. Joseph Cottolengo, pray for us. Teach us to trust in Providence and to care for those no one else will help. Amen.

s307.content:
Marcellin was a French priest who, after sitting with a dying teenage boy who knew nothing of God, resolved to found a congregation of brothers to teach the young.

He founded the Marist Brothers in 1817 and built their first house with his own hands. Today they run schools across the world.
s307.intercession: St. Marcellin, pray for us. Bless teachers, and help every young person to know and love Jesus and Mary. Amen.

s308.content:
Arnold was a German priest and science teacher who, during the anti-Catholic Kulturkampf, founded a missionary seminary just across the border in Steyl, in the Netherlands, in 1875.

He founded the Society of the Divine Word and two congregations of sisters, and started a printing press to spread the faith. His missionaries, including St. Joseph Freinademetz, went to China, Africa, the Americas, and the Pacific.
s308.intercession: St. Arnold Janssen, pray for us. Bless missionaries, and help the Word of God reach every people. Amen.

s309.content:
Luigi was a poor boy from Piedmont who studied under St. John Bosco. As a young priest he founded the Little Work of Divine Providence to serve the poorest and most abandoned.

He rushed to help after the earthquakes of Messina in 1908 and Marsica in 1915, opening orphanages and homes. His congregations now serve in many countries. He was canonized in 2004.
s309.intercession: St. Luigi Orione, pray for us. Make us generous to the poor and quick to help in times of disaster. Amen.

s310.content:
Rafael was a Mexican priest who, during the revolution and the persecution of the Church, disguised himself as a junk dealer, a musician, and a doctor to bring the sacraments to the dying.

As bishop of Veracruz he spent most of his time in hiding or exile, yet kept his seminary running in secret. He gave away everything to the poor. He was canonized in 2006, the first Latin American bishop declared a saint.
s310.intercession: St. Rafael Guízar, pray for us. Strengthen bishops and priests who serve under persecution, and bless seminarians. Amen.

s311.content:
Ursula was an Austrian-born Polish Ursuline nun who went to St. Petersburg to run a boarding school for girls. Expelled from Russia during the First World War, she worked in Scandinavia, where she won respect among Lutherans and helped Polish refugees.

She founded the Grey Ursulines, devoted to education and service to the poor. Her sister, Bl. Maria Teresa Ledóchowska, was also beatified.
s311.intercession: St. Ursula Ledóchowska, pray for us. Bless refugees and teachers, and make us cheerful in serving others. Amen.

s312.content:
Rafael was a cheerful Spanish architecture student and artist who entered the Trappist monastery of San Isidoro de Dueñas at twenty-two. Severe diabetes forced him to leave three times, and he returned each time as a lay oblate.

His writings on "God alone" and on accepting God’s will in suffering have touched many. He died at twenty-seven and was canonized in 2009.
s312.intercession: St. Rafael Arnáiz, pray for us. Help the sick and young people who struggle to find God’s will to say, "God alone." Amen.

s313.content:
Alberto was a Chilean Jesuit who taught that the poor are Christ. In 1944 he founded the Hogar de Cristo, homes for homeless children and adults, often driving his green pickup truck through Santiago at night to find them.

He also founded a labor union movement and a magazine on social questions. Dying of cancer, he kept repeating "Content, Lord, content." He was canonized in 2005.
s313.intercession: St. Alberto Hurtado, pray for us. Help us to see Christ in the poor and to serve Him with joy. Amen.

s314.content:
José Gregorio was a Venezuelan physician and scientist who brought modern medicine and microscope research to Venezuela. He treated the poor for free, often paying for their medicine himself.

Twice he tried to enter religious life but was turned away by ill health. He died after being struck by a car while carrying medicine to a patient. Beloved as "the doctor of the poor," he was canonized in 2025.
s314.intercession: St. José Gregorio Hernández, pray for us. Bless physicians and the sick, and help us to serve the poor generously. Amen.

s315.content:
Bartolo was an Italian lawyer who, as a student, became involved in spiritualism and the occult and despaired of salvation. With the help of a Dominican priest he returned to the faith.

In the ruins of ancient Pompeii he built a shrine to Our Lady of the Rosary, along with orphanages for the children of prisoners. The Shrine of Pompeii became a great pilgrimage site. He was canonized in 2025.
s315.intercession: St. Bartolo Longo, pray for us. Free all who are caught in the occult, and help us to pray the Rosary faithfully. Amen.

s316.content:
Peter was a married lay catechist in Papua New Guinea. When Japanese forces occupied the island during the Second World War and imprisoned the missionaries, he kept the Church alive, leading prayer, baptizing, and preparing couples for marriage.

When the occupiers legalized polygamy, he openly defended Christian marriage. He was arrested and killed in prison by lethal injection. He was canonized in 2025.
s316.intercession: St. Peter To Rot, pray for us. Bless catechists and married couples, and give us courage to defend the dignity of marriage. Amen.

s317.content:
Papias was bishop of Hierapolis in Asia Minor and, according to St. Irenaeus, a hearer of the apostle John and a companion of St. Polycarp. He made it his task to gather everything he could from those who had known the apostles.

His five books, the Expositions of the Sayings of the Lord, are lost, but fragments preserved by Eusebius give some of the earliest testimony about how the Gospels of Mark and Matthew were written.
s317.intercession: St. Papias, pray for us. Help us to treasure the faith handed down from the apostles. Amen.

s318.content:
Melito was bishop of Sardis in Asia Minor and one of the most respected Christian writers of the 2nd century. He traveled to the Holy Land to learn which books belonged to the Old Testament and made the earliest surviving Christian list of them.

His Easter homily, On the Pascha, lost for centuries and rediscovered in the 20th century, is a poetic meditation on Christ as the true Passover Lamb.
s318.intercession: St. Melito, pray for us. Help us to see Christ in all the Scriptures and to celebrate His Passover with joy. Amen.

s319.content:
In 177, a mob in Lyon and Vienne in Gaul turned on the Christians. Pothinus, the city’s first bishop, more than ninety years old, was beaten and died in prison. Dozens of others were tortured and thrown to wild beasts in the amphitheater.

Blandina, a slave girl, astonished her torturers by her endurance, repeating, "I am a Christian, and there is nothing vile done by us." Their story survives in a moving letter preserved by Eusebius.
s319.intercession: Holy martyrs of Lyon, pray for us. Give us courage to confess Christ whatever the cost. Amen.

s320.content:
Theophilus was a pagan convert who became bishop of Antioch, the city where the disciples were first called Christians. His defense of the faith, To Autolycus, was written to a pagan friend.

In it he became the first known writer to use the Greek word for "triad" of God, His Word, and His Wisdom, an early step toward the Church’s language of the Trinity.
s320.intercession: St. Theophilus, pray for us. Help us to explain our faith to our friends with patience and love. Amen.
